question: Does a stationary copper sphere show reproducible mode changes between table positions after controlling fixture, orientation, temperature, excitation and receiver geometry?
target: finite-band mechanical velocity/force FRF, table acceleration PSD and matched modal-frequency differences; environmental channels recorded separately
not_defined: An entire frequency of an object or spatial point is not a single calibrated observable.
model: Homogeneous isotropic, traction-free sphere radial l=0 family; representative effective copper values; measured specimen calibration required.
protocol: Balanced randomized ABBA/BAAB stationary acquisitions, fixed spacing; return-to-A; blank fixture; reference; environmental covariates.
controls: ideal translation leaves free model eigenfrequencies invariant
receiver weights can change peaks without shifting eigenfrequencies
support stiffness can change coupled modes
radius scaling and independent boundary equation
sampling and FFT bin separation not estimator accuracy
no thermal coefficient inferred from expansion alone
acceptance: independent physics derivation and code comparison
model failures and invalid inputs exposed
sources with venue/date/reading-depth and typed graph
functional calculator/network/exports at desktop and mobile
isolated feature branch and reproducible build
provenance: Separate model-agent physics producer, source researcher, experiment skeptic and analysis implementer; root implements the interface, integrates and reviews. No human peer review.
deployment_scope: Isolated page inside devices; no master or archive application changes.
